html:
The Sotho are a Bantu-speaking people of the high grasslands of southern Africa, today mainly in Lesotho and South Africa. The map shows a Sotho territory from 1783 to 1815, though the shape it draws lies far from their real homeland on the highveld.

In those years the Sotho lived in many small chiefdoms, herding cattle and growing sorghum, and built stone-walled villages. Soon after, the wars of the Mfecane, set off as the Zulu kingdom and its rivals expanded, broke many of these chiefdoms apart.

Out of that turmoil the chief Moshoeshoe I gathered refugees at the mountain fortress of Thaba Bosiu from 1824 and built the Basotho nation. He defended it against Boer settlers and asked Britain for protection in 1868, which kept it out of South Africa and made it the state of Lesotho.
